sentences.text: This petition is filed U/Sec.166 of M.V Act claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- together with costs and interest @ 12% p.a, from the date of petition till its realization.

2. Brief Facts of the Petition are as follows: The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 24.09.2021 at about 7.30 p.m, when the petitioner was riding the Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05-U-539 by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and when he reached near 5th Main road junction, HSR Layout, Outer Ring Road, Bengaluru City,
at that time the driver of Goods canter bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-3011 came in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Sakra Hospital, wherein he took first aid and then he was shifted to ESI hospital and then shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent several examinations and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
He stated that he was working as Security guard and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods Canter.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.1 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Goods canter bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-3011.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 147, 149, 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the said accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner and further the petitioner himself riding the motorcycle and bike got skidded and fell down in the night time hence, the petitioner was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Further the petitioner was not possessing valid DL and the said vehicle was not insured at the time of accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings, the tribunal framed following issues:

sentences.text:
1 ) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 24.09.2021 at about 7.30 p.m., near 5th main junction, HSR Layout,
Outer ring road, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Goods canter bearing Reg.No.KA- 41-C-3011 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6.
In order to prove the above issues the petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 12 were marked on his behalf.
Dr.Chidanand.
K.J.C, Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.2 and Ex's.P13 & 14 were marked.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 examined the CMO of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital as RW.1 and through him got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.
Further the respondent No.1 also examined its Senior Manager as RW.2.
Ex.R3 to 6 documents were marked through this witness.
7. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1 : In the Negative Issue No.2 : In the Negative Issue No.3 :
As per final order for the following REASONS 8.
ISSUE NO.1 : The injured in the above case filed evidence affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and reiterated the petition averments.

To corroborate his oral testimony he has produced police documents viz., Ex.P1-FIR, Ex.P2-Complaint, Ex.P3-Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4-Spot Sketch, Ex.P.5-IMV report, Ex.P.6-Charge sheet, Ex.P.7-Wound Certificate and Ex.P.8- Discharge summary.
On his behalf, the petitioner examined orthopedic surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital who was examined as PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner has 11% disability to the whole body.

On the basis of these documents the petitioner tried to impress upon this Tribunal that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Goods Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-3011.
But the point that merits consideration is that charge sheet is not conclusive proof of negligence.

It is incumbent upon this Tribunal to find out the truth independently without relying upon the charge sheet, More so when the very involvement of Goods Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-3011 in the alleged accident is denied by the respondent No.1/ insurance company.

9. Respondent No.1 has mainly relied upon the entries made in Ex.R1- Police intimation of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Ex.R.2-MLC Extract of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Ex.R.3-Discharge summary of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital and police intimation of the petitioner issued by Sakra Hospital to indicate that the injuries sustained by the petitioner were not on account of its insured vehicle.
The contents of Ex.R.1- Police intimation wherein it is mentioned as RTA at 7.30 p.m, on 29.09.2021 near Silk board, HSR Layout, 5th Main.

Further on perusal of Ex.R.2 Accident Information Register of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital it is mentioned as H/o alleged RTA at around 7.30 p.m, on 29.09.2021 near Silk Board while riding a 2 wheeler hit a barricade grills and sustained injuries to both lower limbs.

sentences.text: Further Ex.R.3 being the Discharge summary of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital wherein it is mentioned pre-existing medical conditions and medications on presentation column it is discloses that "Alleged History of Skid and fall from bike around 8 pm Near Silk board, Bengaluru on a two wheeler - sustained injury to B/L Thighs."
The police intimation of Sakra Hospital wherein it is mentioned as A/H/o Skid and fall today at around 7.30 p.m ring road, near Silk board.
During the course of cross examination PW.1 / injured stated that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Sakra Hospital, Bellandur.
Further he stated that based on advise of the doctors of Sakra Hospital, he was shifted to ESI Hospital for further treatment.
Further he stated that he was only taken first aid treatment at Sakra Hospital.
During the course of his cross-examination PW.2 i.e. the doctor stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
He stated that he has not seen any documents of ESI Hospital.
The respondent No.1 examined the CMO of M.S.Ramaiah Hospital as RW.1.
He has produced Ex.R.1 and 2 being the police intimation and accident information Register Extract.
During the course of his cross examination he stated that he do not have any personal knowledge about the accident.
As per the contents of Ex.R.1 he has given intimation to the police from their hospital as RTA.
As per the contents of Ex.R.2, the date of accident is 29.09.2021 and time is 7.30 p.m.
The history mentioned in Ex.R.2 was given the petitioner himself.
He further stated that generally they record the information based on the statement given by the person who had taken or brought the injured to the hospital.
He was the treated doctor in emergency unit.
He further stated that he might have seen the documents to substantiate his say that the patient had taken treatment in Sakra Hospital and ESI Hospital.
Further he stated that only initial emergency treatment was given by him.

10. As per the petitioner's own version, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Sakra Hospital, wherein he took first aid and then he was shifted to ESI hospital and then shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital.
Ex.P8/ Discharge summary of M.S.Ramaiah hospital, goes to show that the petitioner was admitted to the said hospital on 30.09.2021.

The Course in hospital & Major events during admission column therein states that "patient was referred from ESI Hospital with history of RTA with H/O soft tissue injury to the thighs and no H/o Abdomen, chest or head injuries.
Patient had pain and swelling of the right and left thigh.
E-Fast and CECT abdomen showed no evidence of solid organ injury"
11. Be that as it may, no documents are produced pertaining to the admission of the petitioner in Sakra hospital.
No referral letter is produced.
Moreover, no attempt is made to produce the MLC extracts of the said hospital, to show that it was the offending Goods vehicle which was involved in the accident.

Further the petitioner during the course of his cross- examination he categorically admitted that at the time when the signal left, the canter vehicle came at a high speed and dashed against his motorcycle to its rear side.

On perusal of IMV report which is marked at Ex.P.5, wherein it is clearly mentioned that the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-U-0539 sustained front right side body scratched, right side handal steering scratched and right side rear view mirror and brake lever damaged and to the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-3011 no damages found.
Further the petitioner stated that the offending vehicle dashed to the rear side of the motorcycle but in the IMV Report there is no damages to the rear side.
It creates doubt.
12. It is pertinent to note that the petitioner has not made any effort to examine the driver of the offending vehicle to prove the accident.

But for the best reasons known to him, no endeavor was B.R.Venkataramanna vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35771403/
4 made by PW.1 to disprove the contents of Ex.R1 to 3 and evidence of driver of the offending vehicle.
Since there is no contra evidence to show that the entries made in Ex.R1 to 3 are wrong entries, this Tribunal is left with no other alternative than to accept and hold that there is no nexus between the injuries suffered by the petitioner and the alleged accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears that because of this reason only the authorities of Sakra Hospital have not registered the MLC and sent the intimation to the police for registration of the FIR.

13. In order to convert an unfortunate incident into a windfall, the Goods vehicle insured by the respondent No.1 was implicated by lodging a false complaint that too after lapse of 22 hours from the time of occurrence of the alleged accident.
Though it is a settled principle of criminal jurisprudence that mere delay in lodging the complaint may not prove fatal in all cases.
But in the given circumstances of the case, delay of 22 hours in lodging the complaint is one of the factors which erodes the credibility of the petitioner's version.
All these discrepancies fortify the fact that the petitioner did not sustain any injury in any accident involving the Goods vehicle insured by the respondent No.1.
In spite of it the jurisdictional police have filed a false charge sheet against the driver of goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-3011.
If the alleged goods vehicle involved in the accident, the petitioner would have produced MLC and intimation of Sakra Hospital.

To conclude,
the theory put-forth by the claimant that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of the driver of goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C- 3011 is contrary to the evidence on record.
It is a clear case of fraudulent claim made by the petitioner with an oblique intention of wangling an award.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Negative'.
14. ISSUE NO.2 :

In view of the findings arrived at issue No.1, the petitioner failed to prove that he sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of the goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-3011 by its driver.
Rather evidence on record clearly establishes that the petitioner sustained injuries due to his own negligence i.e., on account of 'skid and fall from bike'.
Accordingly when the petitioner himself is the tortfeasor, the claim is not maintainable.

Consequently issue No.2 also deserves to be answered 'In the Negative'.
15. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 and 2 and for the reasons discussed therein , I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby dismissed.
Parties to bear their own costs.
Draw an award accordingly.
